issues.issue: The Schedule states "Additional Ratings Not Applicable" while assigning a 150% substandard Risk Classification, which cannot be squared with the acceptance-form amendment "Base policy is rated" (c168) and with the Monthly Deduction component (d) for Additional Ratings in Section 9.

The notice requires "the Net Policy Value, less Policy Debt" to cover deductions, but Section 3 already defines Net Policy Value as Policy Value less Policy Debt (c026), so debt is deducted twice against the Section 11 lapse test.
The table fixes the Cost of Insurance Charge only by reference to Section 9 and the Section 2 maximum rates, so its meaning depends entirely on the contested rate-setting language in c070/c072.
The Schedule shows a Rider Charge of "None" for the Living Benefit Rider, while the rider itself authorises an Administrative Charge on payment (c155).
The $1,000,000 Maximum Annual Premium sits against Section 4's promise that "in no event will we refuse to accept any premium necessary to prevent the policy from terminating" (c041).

This footnote asserts an unqualified "right to change ... the amount of cost of insurance deducted under the policy," which cannot be squared with Section 9's limits on re-determining COI rates (c072) and its enumerated rate factors (c070).
"We have the right to change ... the amount of cost of insurance" states no standard or limit, leaving open whether the right is unfettered or governed by Section 9.
The 1980 CSO basis fixes only the Section 2 guaranteed maximum rates, leaving its relationship to the current-rate provision in Section 9 (c070) open to argument.

The unisex Monthly Factor is stated as "4.0032737" where the corresponding factor in the same table is 1.0032737, a transcription error that would materially change every Net Amount at Risk calculation.
"Age 100 Anniversary" (Policy Anniversary nearest the 100th birthday) and "Maturity Date" (Attained Age 100, c023) are separately defined and need not fall on the same date.

Defining Attained Age as "the Age plus the number of whole years that have elapsed since the Policy Date" double-counts, because "Age" is itself defined as the current age at the nearest birthday rather than the age at issue.
"Any day that we are open for business" defines the term by reference to the insurer's own unstated practice, giving no ascertainable boundary.
The catch-all "any other proof acceptable to us" follows two specific items and gives the insurer sole say over what suffices, leaving the reach of the definition uncertain.

The definition requires a "written form signed by you, satisfactory to us" but then adds "or such other medium electronic or otherwise that we may from time to time make available," so whether signature and satisfaction are always required is unclear.

The Maturity Date is defined as the date the Insured reaches Attained Age 100, yet Section 8 (c059-c063) provides for continuing coverage, interest crediting and default on or after that date, so nothing actually "matures."
The Schedule notice (c005) speaks of "the Net Policy Value, less Policy Debt," which duplicates the subtraction built into this definition.
The sentence is ungrammatical ("that you intend to be pay on a regular modal basis") and ends without punctuation, though the intended sense is recoverable.
The opening formula credits Net Premium "less an amount not to exceed one month of Monthly Deductions," which fixes only a ceiling and leaves the actual initial deduction indeterminate.
The definition trails off after "less any unpaid issue charges," leaving the sentence incomplete on the face of the instrument.
"We" refers only to the Company here, while the Living Benefit Rider defines "We" as Phoenix "or its subsidiaries" (c145).

"We reserve the right to make any reasonable adjustments to the terms or conditions of this policy ... to the extent we deem it necessary" combines an objective standard ("reasonable") with a subjective one ("we deem") and sets no boundary on what may be adjusted.
The reserved unilateral power to adjust terms sits against Section 22 (c134), which requires any change in the provisions of the policy to be in writing signed and countersigned by officers.

"In no event, however, will we refuse to accept any premium necessary to prevent the policy from terminating" contradicts Section 4's reserved right to refuse premiums failing the elected test (c040) and Section 10's directive not to process such payments (c081).

The Cash Value Accumulation Test terms, including a retroactive right to modify Death Benefit Percentages, are inoperative on their face because Section 1 records the Guideline Premium Test as the elected, unchangeable test.

A pro-rata Surrender Charge is imposed on any face reduction here, whereas Section 6 says a face reduction on a Death Benefit Option change carries "no change to the surrender charge schedule" (c054).

The rule that no Death Proceeds are paid once a surrender request is received depends on Section 15's statement that after receipt "no insurance will be in force" (c111), and neither addresses a request received but not yet processed.

The insurer's right to strip Policy Value or demand insurability is triggered when the Net Amount at Risk "exceeds our guidelines and limitations that may be in effect" — an external, undisclosed and unilaterally variable standard.
The closing text is broken: "You are limited to one surrender charges for this policy" is not a sentence, and the limit on changes per Policy Year has been displaced into a stray heading.
The Monthly Guarantee Premium may be modified on "a change in risk classification," but no mechanism anywhere fixes how the revised premium is computed or when Risk Classification can change.

This makes the post-age-100 Death Benefit the greater of Total Face Amount or Policy Value, dropping the Minimum Death Benefit Percentage multiplier that Section 6 (c053) applies, although Section 8 opens by saying the benefit is determined "in the same respect as specified in Section 6."

"We will not accept any further premium payments" after the Age 100 Anniversary cannot be reconciled with Section 11 (c087), which allows a policy in default to be cured only by additional premiums or debt repayment, and with Section 13 reinstatement.
Post-age-100 default is defined here, but Section 11's cure mechanism (c087) contemplates payment of additional premiums, which c061 forbids after the Age 100 Anniversary.

Component (d) charges for "any applicable Additional Ratings shown in Section 1," but Section 1 records Additional Ratings as "Not Applicable" while the acceptance form states the base policy is rated (c168).

The rating factors listed here (sex, Age, Risk Classification, Basic and Supplemental Face Amount, Net Amount at Risk, duration) are an enumeration whose exclusivity is left open, and "duration that the coverage has been in force" is not tied to any table.

This list of factors for rates "as of the Policy Date" differs from the wholly different list governing rates thereafter in the next paragraph (c070), leaving it unclear which controls a re-determination.

"Such rates will be based on our expectations of future mortality, persistency, investment earnings, expense experience, capital and reserve requirements, and tax assumptions" is an enumerated list with no catch-all, so whether the insurer may set COI rates on factors outside the list — and what "based on" requires — is squarely contestable.
The constrained rate formula here cannot be squared with the Schedule footnote asserting an unqualified "right to change ... the amount of cost of insurance deducted under the policy" (c011).

"On a basis that does not discriminate unfairly within any class of insureds" leaves "class of insureds" undefined and "unfairly" unmeasured, and "we will not ... recoup prior losses" gives no test for when a rate increase does so.
The limits on re-determination stated here are contradicted by the Schedule footnote reserving an unrestricted right to change the cost of insurance deducted (c011).

The crediting sentence is broken mid-line so that the standard ("anticipation of future investment earnings, mortality, persistency, expense and administrative costs, and taxes") floats free of the grant of "sole discretion" to change rates, leaving it unclear whether that standard constrains the discretion.
The Additional Interest table is internally garbled — a middle band of "50%" against a top band of "4.00%" — so the rate actually payable in each band cannot be read off the provision.
The instruction not to process premiums that would disqualify the policy sits against Section 4's promise that "in no event" will a premium needed to prevent termination be refused (c041).

The middle of the paragraph is unreadable ("Unless we agree oth ===gre-subject-to-the-Maximum-Annual-Premium-shol 6 Overloan Protection"), so the Maximum Annual Premium limit and the Overloan cut-off cannot be stated from the text.
This debt-based default and its premium cure must be read with Section 8 (c061), which bars acceptance of any premium after the Age 100 Anniversary while expressly keeping default alive.

The opening of the Reduced Paid-Up Benefit is destroyed ("-after-this.policy.has..been..in-force.for.at.least.one.full ~=lapsed-to-a- -"), so the conditions for and nature of the election cannot be determined from the provision.
The exclusive list of automatic termination events omits the Maturity Date, although Section 1 fixes a Maturity Date of October 12, 2035 and Section 3 defines it as a policy term.

The provision begins mid-sentence ("request. A loan may not be taken after you have exercised Overloan Protecti"), so the operative grant of the right to take a loan and its conditions are missing from the text.

"A change in the Interest Rate" is capitalised but undefined, and could mean the credited interest rate under Section 9 or the policy loan interest rate under the surrounding Loan Interest Charged provision.

The right to repay Policy Debt "at any time prior to the death of the Insured and while the policy is in force" conflicts with the Overloan Protection bullet stating that no loan repayments will be allowed (c108).

Condition 2 requires that the Policy Debt "is equal to 96% of the Policy Value," a knife-edge test that cannot be squared with the next paragraph's assumption that the loan balance may be "in excess of 96% of the Policy Value" when the option is exercised (c101).
Ceasing all monthly deductions on Overloan Protection has to be reconciled with Section 9's rule that deductions are due on every Monthly Calculation Date until the Age 100 Anniversary (c067).

"No additional loans or loan repayments will be allowed" contradicts the Loan Repayment provision permitting repayment at any time while the policy is in force (c099), and sits oddly with c101's requirement that excess loan balance be repaid on exercise.

The provision imposes a one-time Overloan Transaction Charge and then trails off mid-sentence with "There is no additional charge for this benefit or for any of the automatic", leaving the charge scheme incomplete on its face.

"After we receive your written request to surrender the policy, no insurance will be in force" works with Section 6's denial of Death Proceeds after a surrender request (c046) but neither says what happens if the request is later withdrawn or rejected.

Condition (c) refers to "the Minimum Face Amount shown in Section 1," but Section 1 states only a Minimum Total Face Amount and a Minimum Basic Face Amount (c010), so the referenced figure does not exist.

The right-of-first-refusal bar on transfers for consideration has no time limit, no price mechanism and turns on "information satisfactory to us," so what defeats a transfer of ownership is left at large.
This restriction on transfers for consideration is hard to square with Section 18, which lets the owner assign any interest by written notice without anyone's consent (c123).

The text is broken mid-provision ("Gonsent-of-any-~beneficiary... s.not.reauired..f.there.is..no0 'Insured, your estate will be the Beneficiary'"), so the default-beneficiary rule and the consent rule cannot be read as sentences.
Payment "in equal shares" to surviving beneficiaries has to be reconciled with the application's "% Share" designation (c176), which contemplates unequal shares.

The freedom to "assign any interest in this policy without the consent of any person other than an irrevocable Beneficiary" is qualified only by "except as otherwise provided," and Section 17 (c119) blocks collateral or absolute assignments for consideration.
The adjustment is to be made "by the most recent Cost of Insurance charge deducted under Section 9," a phrase that does not state a workable formula for recomputing the face amount.

The opening of the incontestability clause is missing ("the Issue Date, except' for-any™p insurability"), so the length of the basic contestable period and its exception cannot be read from the provision.
A payment "limited to the higher of" two amounts reads as a floor rather than the cap the sentence purports to impose, so the measure of recovery on a contested face amount is uncertain.

The integration clause is immediately undercut by "such additional requests may become part of the policy," which conflicts with Section 22's requirement that any change be in writing signed and countersigned by officers (c134).
The signed-writing requirement for any change is contradicted by Section 4's reserved right to make unilateral "reasonable adjustments to the terms or conditions" of the policy (c040).
"Clerical errors" is undefined and the correction right is unilateral, so the line between correcting a slip and altering a term is left to the insurer.
The opening obligation is unreadable ("nniversary-we:will:send-you=-without-charge ach-Policy Year which-ineludes"), so the timing and trigger of the annual statement cannot be stated from the text.

A fee of up to $50 for a report requested "at any other time" sits against the next paragraph's promise of "one report annually without charge" (c138), leaving overlapping and inconsistent charging rules.
Defining "We" as Phoenix "or its subsidiaries" for rider purposes departs from Section 3, where "we" refers only to the Company (c038), leaving the obligor under the rider unclear.
Limitation 3 forbids a Requested Benefit "less than the lower of 25% of the policy face amount or $50,000," a double comparative that is awkward to apply against limitation 4's separate cap.

"Expected to result in the insured's death within six months based on evidence satisfactory to us" combines a prognosis judgment with the insurer's own satisfaction, and gives no objective standard for either.
"There is no premium charge for this rider" has to be reconciled with the rider's deduction of a "then current Administrative Charge" of up to $300 from the accelerated payment (c155).
"Our discounting rate will be subject to the higher of: 1. 5%; or 2. the Published Monthly Average" does not say whether that higher figure is a floor or a ceiling on the rate the insurer may apply.
The sentence is fragmentary ("The discounted del any other 5 then current Administrative Charge"), so what is subtracted from the discounted benefit cannot be determined from the words.
The enumerated list of values "reduced by the Proportion" is scrambled ("Oo PWN") and includes policy debt, so which items are reduced, and in what order, is not readable from the provision.

The subaccount mechanics presuppose a variable life policy, whereas this contract is a fixed universal life policy with a Guaranteed Minimum Interest Rate (c010), making the paragraph inoperative here.
"Any creditor, trustee in bankruptcy or governmental agency, or arising under any court order directed against you" is a mixed list whose general reach against ordinary assignees is left uncertain.
"Home Office approval of form #519B is necessary before the policy is in effect" adds a condition of effectiveness not found in Section 10 (c080) or the application's own list of conditions (c190).
"Base policy is rated" cannot be squared with the Schedule Page entry "Additional Ratings Not Applicable" (c004), which controls the Section 9 Monthly Deduction component for ratings.
The paragraph's clauses are interleaved and unreadable ("payments wili ha shared equally by all primary ben beneilelarles who survive..."), so the default sharing rule cannot be read off the text.
The face amount applied for is illegible and does not match the $6,000,000 recorded by the amendment (c172) and the Schedule Page (c004).
The premium figures shown in the application do not match the amendment's first-year and subsequent planned annual premium of $299,526 (c170, c171) or the Schedule's Planned Premium.
The application's five conditions for insurance to take effect, including payment in full during the insured's lifetime, are not the same conditions stated in Section 10 of the policy (c080).
